title: How Many Things I Do Not Need
title_html:
How Many Things
I Do Not Need
source: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Philosophers II.25 (Yonge tr.)
lines: Socrates loved walking through the Athens market. Gold jewellery, silk robes, fancy perfume, exotic spices. Everything sparkled.
The merchants shouted, Buy this! You need this! Special price, today only!
Socrates looked at everything very carefully, even picking up a golden necklace. And bought nothing.
A friend caught up with him. Why do you come here, if you never buy anything?
Socrates smiled. I come to see how many things there are that I don't need.
His friend looked down at his twelve shopping bags. And said nothing.
The richest person isn't the one who has the most. It's the one who needs the least. Socrates walked home with empty hands, and a very full mind.
Next time: Socrates' wife, and a bucket of water. Follow so you don't miss it!
